question: What did the actual customers say in the calls supporting that conclusion?

answer.answer_markdown:
**Customers do not say the bank was wrong to act - they say nobody would tell them why.** That refusal is the complaint, in 407 contacts carrying 417 distinct wordings. Here is the shape of it, in their words.

The plainest version, from a checking customer in June 2026: "I have never committed fraud or any illegal activity on these accounts or any money laundering. I asked for a reason and they wouldn't tell me anything. They just closed the accounts." An auto loan customer in August 2024 put it in seven words: "Chase refused to give me that information." And a checking customer in December 2024: "I was told i was not allowed to do business eith chase. No other explanation."

A second strand is customers who did everything asked of them and were stopped anyway. From a wire in January 2025: "In this call, I passed the security review, yet I was given a reason that my fund was insufficient. My wire was hence cancelled." From a credit card in November 2025: "Despite this, Chase has repeatedly placed improper security holds and declined legitimate transactions for both me and my AU, even after multiple successful identity verifications." From a mortgage in September 2025: "my agreed upon payment would not be accepted because of potential fraud and equity theft"

A third strand is what the closures cost people while the reason stays unstated. October 2025: "Chase bank closed my account today without telling me why and I had $22.00 in there too buy food today." December 2025: "Chase froze one of my checking accounts with XXXX balance XXXX months ago without any letter explaining on why or what I can do to get my funds back." April 2025: "They will not tell me why they are terminating this relationship nor have they provided a timeline during which I can expect account closure." And in April 2026 the customer's complaint was not the closure at all but the record of it: "Chase refused to put the time and date of the account closure."

The words are consistent across 7 products and 25 months, average sentiment -1.28, and 275 of the 407 contacts are checking and savings. One caveat on the words themselves: 404 of the 407 are written complaints, so this is what customers wrote, not what they said out loud. XXXX in the text is the regulator's own redaction of names, dates and amounts.

claims.statement: Across 407 contacts carrying 417 distinct wordings, customers' own statements describe accounts closed, frozen or restricted with the reason withheld, and it is the withholding rather than the action that they complain about.

quotes.why: June 2026, checking and savings: the complaint in its purest form - no fraud, no reason, account gone.

quotes.quote: Chase refused to give me that information.
quotes.why: August 2024, auto loan: the oldest end of the range, and the whole theme in seven words.

quotes.quote: my Chase Sapphire card said CLOSED! Their reason was " Due to multiple card 's opened along with the Chase Sapphire, they claim that I was abusing my cards ''
quotes.why: May 2025, credit card: a reason was given, but the customer disputes it as an unexplained label.

quotes.quote: my agreed upon payment would not be accepted because of potential fraud and equity theft
quotes.why: September 2025, mortgage: a fraud flag blocking a payment the customer had already agreed.

quotes.quote: In this call, I passed the security review, yet I was given a reason that my fund was insufficient. My wire was hence cancelled.
quotes.why: January 2025, transfers: identity verified, wire cancelled anyway, with a reason the customer says was wrong.

quotes.quote: I was told the accounts could not be reopened because they believed the caller had properly verified my identity.
quotes.why: July 2025, debt collection: the bank's own verification judgement used to keep the accounts shut.

quotes.quote: I was told i was not allowed to do business eith chase. No other explanation.
quotes.why: December 2024, checking and savings: the refusal to explain stated plainly.

quotes.why: October 2025, checking and savings: what a closure with no notice actually costs someone that day.

caveats: The index holds two corpora: 4,425 real written complaints about one bank (July 2024 to June 2026) and 1,000 synthetic agent/customer phone conversations (September 2023 only). The 407 figure covers both.
For this theme 404 of the 407 contacts are written complaints and 3 are synthetic conversations, so despite the word 'calls' these are written statements, not spoken transcripts.
XXXX in the quotes is the regulator's own redaction of names, dates and dollar amounts in the published complaint text. It is not missing data on our side.
Each quote is one customer's account of what happened, recorded as they told it. The index does not establish whether the bank in fact had a valid reason it was barred from disclosing.

sql.sql: SELECT * FROM themes WHERE theme_id = ?
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1
SELECT tc.call_id, c.date, c.week, c.month, c.region FROM v_theme_calls tc JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = tc.call_id WHERE tc.theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY c.date

SELECT t.driver_category, COUNT(DISTINCT t.call_id) AS n FROM theme_members tm JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = tm.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1 GROUP BY t.driver_category ORDER BY n DESC
SELECT t.driver, t.call_id FROM theme_members tm JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = tm.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1
SELECT w.rank, w.issue_statement, w.call_id, w.date, w.product FROM theme_wordings w JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = w.call_id WHERE w.theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY w.rank LIMIT 12
SELECT c.product AS value, COUNT(*) AS n_slice FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY value
SELECT c.product AS value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.call_id) AS n FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY value
SELECT DISTINCT c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ?
SELECT c.channel AS value, COUNT(*) AS n_slice FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY value
SELECT c.channel AS value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.call_id) AS n FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY value
SELECT DISTINCT c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ?
SELECT c.week AS period, COUNT(*) AS n FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY period ORDER BY period
SELECT c.week AS period, c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY period, c.call_id

SELECT m.from_theme, f.name AS from_name, m.into_theme, m.pass, m.reason, m.judged_by, m.created_at FROM theme_merges m JOIN themes f ON f.theme_id = m.from_theme WHERE m.into_theme = ? OR f.effective_theme_id = ? ORDER BY m.created_at, m.from_theme
SELECT * FROM emerging_scores WHERE entity_type = 'theme' AND entity_id = ? AND as_of_week = ?
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

SELECT e.evidence_id, e.call_id, c.date, c.month, c.product, c.region, c.region_group, c.channel, c.segment, t.sentiment, e.quote, e.speaker, t.topic_label, t.driver, e.char_start, e.char_end, e.match_kind FROM evidence e JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = e.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id JOIN theme_members tm ON tm.topic_id = t.topic_id WHERE e.verified = 1 AND tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY ABS(t.sentiment) DESC, c.date DESC, e.evidence_id
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE c.date >= ? AND c.date <= ?

SELECT e.evidence_id, e.call_id, c.date, c.month, c.product, c.region, c.region_group, c.channel, c.segment, t.sentiment, e.quote, e.speaker, t.topic_label, t.driver, e.char_start, e.char_end, e.match_kind FROM evidence e JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = e.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id JOIN theme_members tm ON tm.topic_id = t.topic_id WHERE e.verified = 1 AND tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND c.date >= ? AND c.date <= ? ORDER BY ABS(t.sentiment) DESC, c.date DESC, e.evidence_id
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE c.date >= ? AND c.date <= ?

SELECT e.evidence_id, e.call_id, c.date, c.month, c.product, c.region, c.region_group, c.channel, c.segment, t.sentiment, e.quote, e.speaker, t.topic_label, t.driver, e.char_start, e.char_end, e.match_kind FROM evidence e JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = e.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id JOIN theme_members tm ON tm.topic_id = t.topic_id WHERE e.verified = 1 AND tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND c.date >= ? AND c.date <= ? ORDER BY ABS(t.sentiment) DESC, c.date DESC, e.evidence_id

SELECT th.theme_id, th.name, th.problem_statement, th.root_cause, th.polarity, th.driver_category, th.n_wordings, th.n_products, COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') AS grouping_quality, th.first_seen_week, es.status AS status_at_as_of, es.emerging_score, COUNT(DISTINCT s.call_id) AS n_calls, SUM(CASE WHEN s.min_sentiment < 0 THEN -s.min_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS neg_mass, SUM(CASE WHEN s.max_sentiment > 0 THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS pos_mass, AVG(CASE WHEN th.polarity = 'positive' THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE s.min_sentiment END) AS mean_sentiment FROM themes th JOIN v_theme_call_sentiment s ON s.theme_id = th.theme_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = s.call_id LEFT JOIN emerging_scores es ON es.entity_type = 'theme' AND es.entity_id = th.theme_id AND es.as_of_week = ? WHERE 1=1 AND th.status = 'active' AND COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') != 'weak' GROUP BY th.theme_id HAVING n_calls >= ? ORDER BY n_calls DESC, th.theme_id LIMIT ?
SELECT tc.theme_id, tc.call_id FROM v_theme_calls tc JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = tc.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND tc.theme_id IN (?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ORDER BY c.date DESC, tc.call_id
